label: Lifetime cannabis use
description: Have you ever used cannabis?
notes: Lifetime cannabis-use indicator.
value_coding: 0 = No; 1 = Yes

label: Age at first cannabis use
description: How old were you when you first used cannabis?
notes: Source eligibility: participants reporting lifetime cannabis use; the all-participant model therefore uses the observed eligible sample without structural zero coding. The descriptive table reports its run-specific non-missing denominator.
value_coding: Age in years

label: Current cannabis use
description: In the past 6 months, have you used cannabis for medical purposes (to treat disease or improve symptoms) or recreational purposes, including use without formal medical authorization?
notes: A past-3-month interval was used for waves separated by 3 months.
value_coding: 0 = No; 1 = Yes

label: CUDIT frequency
description: CUDIT-R frequency score comprising items 1 and 2.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: Summed score, 0–8; higher scores indicate more frequent cannabis use

label: CUDIT problem
description: CUDIT-R problem score comprising items 3 through 8.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates. The source table called this the severity score.
value_coding: Summed score, 0–24; higher scores indicate more cannabis-related problems

label: MPT breakpoint
description: First price increment at which no cannabis would be purchased or consumed.
notes: Marijuana Purchase Task breakpoint; non-users remain missing. Recomputed from the raw non-negative parameter at run time.
value_coding: log1p(raw breakpoint)

label: MPT intensity
description: Cannabis consumption when cannabis is free.
notes: Marijuana Purchase Task curve-derived intensity (Q0); non-users remain missing. Recomputed from the raw non-negative parameter at run time.
value_coding: log1p(raw intensity)

label: MPT Omax
description: Maximum cannabis expenditure across the Marijuana Purchase Task price series.
notes: Marijuana Purchase Task Omax; non-users remain missing. Recomputed from the raw non-negative parameter at run time.
value_coding: log1p(raw Omax)

label: MPT Pmax
description: Price associated with maximum total cannabis expenditure.
notes: Marijuana Purchase Task curve-derived Pmax (unit elasticity); non-users remain missing. Recomputed from the raw non-negative parameter at run time.
value_coding: log1p(raw Pmax)

label: MPT alpha
description: Sensitivity of cannabis consumption to increases in price.
notes: Marijuana Purchase Task elasticity parameter (alpha); non-users remain missing. Recomputed from the raw non-negative parameter at run time.
value_coding: log1p(raw alpha)

label: Monthly cannabis expenditure
description: In the last 6 months, how much do you typically spend on cannabis each month?
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: Monthly expenditure; non-negative continuous value

label: MMM Enhancement
description: Marijuana Motives Measure enhancement subscale.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: 0–20; higher scores indicate stronger enhancement motives

label: MMM Conformity
description: Marijuana Motives Measure conformity subscale.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: 0–20; higher scores indicate stronger conformity motives

label: MMM Expansion
description: Marijuana Motives Measure expansion subscale.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: 0–20; higher scores indicate stronger expansion motives

label: MMM Coping
description: Marijuana Motives Measure coping subscale.
notes: Items 1, 4, 6, and 17 are summed and prorated by 5/4; confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: 0–20; higher scores indicate stronger coping motives

label: MMM Social
description: Marijuana Motives Measure social subscale.
notes: Confirmed non-users receive structural zero in the all-participant primary model; genuine user missingness remains missing; current-user results are effect-size-only sensitivity estimates.
value_coding: 0–20; higher scores indicate stronger social motives

label: Medical cannabis acceptability
description: How socially acceptable do you think it is for a person to use cannabis regularly for medical purposes?
notes: The source response 5 = No opinion is recoded as missing before all analyses.
value_coding: 1 = Completely acceptable; 2 = Somewhat acceptable; 3 = Somewhat unacceptable; 4 = Completely unacceptable; No opinion = missing

label: Recreational cannabis acceptability
description: How socially acceptable do you think it is for a person to use cannabis regularly for non-medical purposes?
notes: The source response 5 = No opinion is recoded as missing before all analyses.
value_coding: 1 = Completely acceptable; 2 = Somewhat acceptable; 3 = Somewhat unacceptable; 4 = Completely unacceptable; No opinion = missing

label: Trying cannabis acceptability
description: How do you feel about adults trying cannabis once or twice for non-medical or recreational purposes?
notes: Higher scores indicate greater disapproval.
value_coding: 1 = Strongly approve; 2 = Somewhat approve; 3 = Neither approve nor disapprove; 4 = Somewhat disapprove; 5 = Strongly disapprove

label: Perceived weekly cannabis harm
description: How much do people risk harming themselves physically and in other ways when they use cannabis once or twice a week?
notes: Higher scores indicate greater perceived harm.
value_coding: 1 = No risk; 2 = Slight risk; 3 = Moderate risk; 4 = Great risk

label: Perceived cannabis risk count
description: Count of endorsed perceived risks of cannabis use.
notes: Options included no risks, legal problems, addiction, impaired memory, increased use of other drugs, personal or relationship problems, decreased intelligence, decreased energy, new or worsening health problems, increased stress/anxiety/depression, disrupted sleep, and other.
value_coding: Count of endorsed risk options, 0–12

label: Perceived cannabis benefit count
description: Count of endorsed perceived benefits of cannabis use.
notes: Options included no benefits, pain management, treatment of disease, relief from stress/anxiety/depression, improved appetite, improved sleep, help decreasing other medicines, improved creativity, improved focus, increased energy, and other. The source table used the singular name cannabis_benefit; the analysis variable is cannabis_benefits.
value_coding: Count of endorsed benefit options, 0–11

label: Impact on friendships / social life
description: During the past 6 months, what type of effect did your cannabis use have on your friendships or social life?
notes: Current-user outcome. In the finalized pipeline, non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing; this supersedes the supplied legacy neutral-value-of-3 note.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Impact on physical health
description: During the past 6 months, what type of effect did your cannabis use have on your physical health?
notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Impact on physical mobility
description: During the past 6 months, what type of effect did your cannabis use have on your physical mobility?
notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Impact on home life / marriage
description: During the past 6 months, what type of effect did your cannabis use have on your home life or marriage?
notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Impact on work / studies

notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Impact on quality of life

notes: Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: 1 = Very positive effect; 2 = Positive effect; 3 = No effect; 4 = Negative effect; 5 = Very negative effect

label: Acute subjective effects summed score
description: Complete sum of 14 acute subjective-effect items assessing changes in consciousness, dry mouth, dizziness, headache, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, visual disturbance, appetite change, coordination and cognitive difficulties, paranoia, and visual or auditory hallucinations when using cannabis.
notes: Participants endorsing medical or recreational cannabis use rated each consequence. Current-user outcome; non-users and genuine missing responses remain missing.
value_coding: Each item: 1 = None, 2 = Minimal, 3 = Mild, 4 = Moderate, 5 = Intense; complete 14-item sum, 14–70
